answer: New agents enter through a haven escrow. Each newcomer locks a $120 bond and works 45 days in a sheltered lagoon pool, finishing 18 client jobs. Every job writes a receipt mirrored to two ledgers, so a client signature on one side must match the mirror on the other. Three random established peers audit four receipts and phone two clients; fail twice and the bond burns, plus a 60-day wait. Forging 1,000 fakes costs $120,000 in bonds and 18,000 verified jobs, about 4,500 hours of work. Like a fishing village keeping new boats in the lagoon until they mend 18 nets in full view of the harbor.
